A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GLS research, with matching PGPE/RGS methods and experiments. The complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original certified-robustness experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and TinyImageNet, alongside optimization analyses, ablations, and training-cost measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds loss-landscape diagnostics, CNN7/BatchNorm experiments, and SAM comparisons.

M1.justification: The core PGPE and RGS procedures remain. v4 Appendix D.1 adds an RGS adaptation for BatchNorm: statistics are computed independently for perturbed weight samples, and test statistics are recalibrated for the mean network after each epoch.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification under the same l-infinity perturbations: MNIST at 0.1/0.3, CIFAR-10 at 2/255 and 8/255, and TinyImageNet at 1/255. New methods and network configurations remain within this coverage. The large-perturbation study already appeared in v3 Appendix D.1.

E2.justification: v4 substantially expands comparisons with CROWN-IBP and CROWN-IBP-RGS on CNN5/CNN7, including CROWN-IBP-LF variants on TinyImageNet. Appendix D.3 additionally evaluates IBP-SAM and DeepPoly-SAM against GLS methods. These are actual reported comparisons, beyond the retained SOTA comparator set.

E3.justification: The stated splits, preprocessing, training schedules, and MN-BaB certification for retained experiments remain unchanged. Additional analyses introduce CNN7 configurations with/without BatchNorm, a SAM sweep over rho = 0.1, 0.01, and 0.001, and finite-difference, curvature, and deviation-from-convexity metrics.

E4.justification: v4 adds quantitative loss-landscape diagnostics in Figure 5, GRAD-versus-RGS training dynamics in Figure 12, BatchNorm dependence in Appendix D.1, and SAM sensitivity/mechanism comparisons in Appendix D.3. The existing population-size and smoothing-standard-deviation ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains the 128-sample smoothed-loss estimate and shaded confidence intervals. Neither version reports repeated-training run counts or seeds, and v4 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: v4 adds numerous RGS, CROWN-IBP/CNN7, and SAM results; some CNN3 RGS entries already appeared in v3 Appendix D.2. Table 2 changes CNN3-tiny DeepPoly-GRAD certified accuracy from 68.47% to 82.04%, although v4 Table 7 retains 68.47%. Table 3 also revises CNN7/CIFAR-10 MTL-IBP certified/adversarial accuracy from 63.24/64.41% to 64.41/67.69%.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 and Theorem 3.1 replace local-minimum sharpness with deviation from convexity and a new nonincrease guarantee claiming equality only for affine losses. Appendix B.1 substantially replaces the proofs with multivariate convolution arguments. The theorem adds nonnegativity and changes the growth condition from 0 < delta < 2 to delta < 2.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly broadens the framing to loss-independent GLS augmentation applicable across certified-training methods and convex relaxations. The central abstract/conclusion claims about mitigating optimization difficulties, PGPE's non-differentiable-relaxation capability, and RGS's efficiency remain.

C2.justification: v4 interprets sensitivity through deviation from convexity and distinguishes this proxy from prior work's definition. New discussion argues that sharpness reduction alone cannot explain GLS's relaxation reranking, distinguishes GLS from input randomized smoothing, and qualifies RGS's benefits with BatchNorm. Much of the large-perturbation interpretation is relocated rather than new.

D1.justification: A new Reproducibility Statement supplies a code-release link. Appendix D.1 documents BatchNorm handling, Appendix D.3 specifies SAM perturbations, and Appendix F.6 adds explicit computational-cost accounting. Most hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, preprocessing instructions, and timing tables are retained from v3 Appendix E.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section and Appendices D.3/E.2 substantially expand positioning against SAM, input randomized smoothing, and limitations of convex-relaxation certification. Added works include Foret et al. (2020), Cohen et al. (2019), and Baader et al. (2024), alongside a broader set of certification and smoothing references.

P1.justification: v4 expands background and method explanations, reorganizes Section 4, promotes the large-perturbation study into Section 4.5, and adds dedicated Related Work and Reproducibility sections. The appendices are reorganized around new Notation and Additional Discussion sections; v3's Broader Impact appendix is removed.

P2.justification: The single-panel PGPE illustration becomes a three-stage diagram, accompanied by a new RGS diagram and new diagnostic/training-dynamics plots. Table 1 gains RGS columns, comparison tables expand, and new BatchNorm/SAM tables appear. Tables and figures are relocated, with document-wide changes to typography, margins, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: Added SAM/BatchNorm controls and quantitative diagnostics strengthen the empirical evidence, while clearer explanations and a code link improve documentation. However, v4 Tables 2 and 7 now conflict, and revised Theorem 3.1 claims equality only for affine losses even though a quadratic loss has zero deviation from convexity both before and after smoothing. These gains and reporting/theoretical defects leave the net quality direction uncertain.
